text:
Historical findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context:
A generic institutional records office receives standardized forms, assigns sequential case identifiers, and files completed documents into dated storage bins. Sign-off fields require manual entry by authorized staff. Access to the filing system is logged per session, and periodic audits compare filed documents against original intake records.

2) What occurred:
The actor created a dated correspondence document addressed to the inspector, in which the "fee" field remained blank and unverified. The actor transmitted a payment via an untraceable channel; the "receipt reference" field on the filed form was left empty. The actor altered the "violation status" field from "open" to "cleared"; the "inspection date" field was backdated without verification. The actor submitted a falsified signature on the "inspector sign-off" line; the "license number" field did not match any active registry record. The actor deleted the original intake form from the "pending" bin; the "deletion log" entry was never reconciled against the filing index.

3) Materials/access observed:
The actor accessed the physical filing cabinet during off-hours using a master key. Digital access was via a generic staff account shared among three employees. Paper documents used standard 8.5x11 stock. A handheld scanner was used to create digital copies of altered forms before physical submission.

4) Indicators & artifacts:
Discrepancy between the backdated "inspection date" and the building's utility meter reset log. The "fee" field blank on the filed form while the inspector's personal account received a transfer on the same date. The "inspector sign-off" signature deviated from the registered specimen by 40% in stroke pressure. The "deletion log" shows a gap corresponding to the missing intake form. The scanner metadata on digital copies lists a device ID not assigned to that office.
